faqs.a: Save it as manifest.webmanifest (or manifest.json) in your site root and reference it from every page's <head>: <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">. Serve it with the MIME type application/manifest+json.
faqs.q: Where do I put the manifest file?

faqs.a: Use both: the Web App Manifest Generator builds the file, then the PWA Manifest Checker validates it against installability requirements. Generate here, verify there.
faqs.q: Should I use this or the PWA Manifest Checker?

faqs.a: The installability minimum: name (or short_name), start_url, display standalone/fullscreen/minimal-ui, and 192px + 512px icons. This generator warns you if any are missing, and pre-fills the icon entries.
faqs.q: What is the minimum for an installable PWA?

faqs.a: start_url is where the app opens when launched from the home screen (usually "/"). scope limits which URLs count as part of your app — links outside it open in the browser. id uniquely identifies the app; set it explicitly so URL changes don't create duplicate installs.
faqs.q: What are start_url, scope, and id?

faqs.a: Android adaptive icons crop icons into shapes, so a maskable variant with padding is recommended. This generator pre-fills the 512px icon with purpose "any maskable" — just point it at your maskable file.
faqs.q: Do I need a maskable icon?

faqs.a: Yes — paste the generated JSON into the PWA Manifest Checker on this site to validate it. Also confirm the <link> tag is in your HTML, the file is served over HTTPS, and you have a registered service worker.

web-app-manifest-generator.formula:
Generated manifest structure:
{
  "name": "…", "short_name": "…",
  "start_url": "/", "scope": "/", "id": "/",
  "display": "standalone | fullscreen | minimal-ui | browser",
  "orientation": "any | natural | landscape | portrait | …",
  "theme_color": "#…", "background_color": "#…",
  "lang": "en", "dir": "ltr | rtl | auto",
  "icons": [{ "src": "…", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png", "purpose": "any maskable" }]
}
Only non-empty fields are included.
howTo: Fill in your app name and short name (at least one is required).
Set the start URL, display mode, theme and background colors.
Adjust or add icon entries — 192px and 512px PNGs are the installability minimum.
Watch the warnings and fix anything flagged.
Copy or download manifest.webmanifest and link it from your HTML.
keyFacts: A Web App Manifest is a JSON file describing your app: name, icons, colors, and launch behavior.
Browsers need name/short_name, start_url, a valid display mode, and 192px + 512px icons before offering installation.
display: standalone gives an app-like window; fullscreen removes all browser UI; minimal-ui keeps basic controls.
theme_color tints the OS UI; background_color fills the splash screen during launch.
The file must be linked from your HTML: <link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">.
Pair with a service worker over HTTPS for a fully installable PWA.

labels.warnBadBg: The background color is not a valid CSS color and was left out.
labels.warnBadTheme: The theme color is not a valid CSS color and was left out.
labels.warnNoName: Neither name nor short_name is set — one is required.

limitations: Generates the manifest file only — you still need the <link> tag, HTTPS, and a service worker.
Cannot create or resize your icon images — point it at real hosted PNG files.
Color inputs are validated as CSS colors, but the file isn't tested against a live browser here.
Unusual manifest fields beyond the common set aren't covered by the form.

web-app-manifest-generator.workedExample:
Inputs: name Example Tools, short_name ExTools, start_url /, display standalone, theme_color #4f46e5, background_color #ffffff, icons /icons/icon-192.png (192x192) and /icons/icon-512.png (512x512, purpose any maskable).
Generated manifest.webmanifest:
{
  "name": "Example Tools",
  "short_name": "ExTools",
  "start_url": "/",
  "display": "standalone",
  "theme_color": "#4f46e5",
  "background_color": "#ffffff",
  "icons": [
    {
      "src": "/icons/icon-192.png",
      "sizes": "192x192",
      "type": "image/png"
    },
    {
      "src": "/icons/icon-512.png",
      "sizes": "512x512",
      "type": "image/png",
      "purpose": "any maskable"
    }
  ]
}
Empty fields (description, scope, id, orientation, dir) are omitted. No warnings — name, 192px, and 512px are all present.
